findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key copies the integer Paginator logic and crashes on datetime ordering
findings.body: The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `getattr(item, 'datetime')`, which is a `datetime`. That raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls the key function on the first result, so any `?optimized_pagination=true` request with at least one row returns a 500. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw cursor value instead of converting the timestamp back to a datetime, as `DateTimePaginator` does. On later pages the WHERE clause would then compare the datetime column to a raw integer. The new path has to reuse `DateTimePaginator`'s conversion (`strftime('%s.%f') * multiplier`) to work at all.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing is not supported by Django QuerySets; the 'advanced feature' only produces errors
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` rejects negative indexes ("Negative indexing is not supported"), so this raises and returns a 500. The comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' and 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' are wrong. A very negative offset also makes `stop` negative, which fails the same way. Cursor strings are user-controlled (`Cursor.from_string` accepts `int(bits[1])`), so any caller who can pass the gate can trigger this on demand. If a backend ever did accept it, the feature would let callers read rows outside the intended page window. Nothing validates or bounds the offset.

findings.title: Permission expression is evaluated on every request and can raise when member is None
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` runs unconditionally, even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested. `organization_context.member` can be `None` for non-members, for example a non-member caller authenticated via a token or API key. For a non-superuser in that case it raises `AttributeError`, which turns previously working audit log requests on the default path into 500s. The check should be evaluated lazily, only when `use_optimized` is true, and should guard against `member is None`.

findings.title: Behavior change in shared BasePaginator.get_result with a misleading comment
findings.body: `BasePaginator.get_result` is used by many endpoints, and this edit changes it. Non-prev cursors with a negative offset are now silently clamped to 0, so a malformed cursor returns the first page instead of failing. Prev cursors still pass the negative offset straight to the queryset, which fails, so the claim that this 'allows negative offsets' and that the queryset 'will handle boundary conditions' is false. `offset` and `start_offset` now differ in the non-prev case, but the later `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check still uses `offset`. The change is unrelated to the audit log feature, risks regressions elsewhere, and should be reverted or properly validated (reject negative offsets with a `BadPaginationError`).

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result wholesale; the 'else' branch is identical to the base
findings.body: The class copy-pastes the whole of `get_result`. Only the negative-offset branch differs, and that branch cannot work (see the negative-slicing finding). The `else` branch is identical to the modified base logic. The result is two parallel implementations that can drift apart. The docstring's claims of 'optimized query path' and 'streamlined boundary condition handling' are not backed by any code, since the query is the same as the base class's.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported but no code change backs it
findings.body: The added comment says the `Cursor` constructor now 'allows negative offsets ... for efficient reverse pagination'. The constructor is unchanged (`int(offset)` already accepted negatives) and nothing downstream supports negative offsets. The comment misleads future maintainers about a capability that does not exist.

findings.title: No tests for the new paginator or the new endpoint branch
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator, a new query-param-gated code path and a change to the shared `BasePaginator`, with no tests. A basic test of `?optimized_pagination=true` would have exposed the datetime `get_item_key` crash, and a negative-offset cursor test would have exposed the slicing error. There is also no coverage of the permission gating (superuser, global access, no member).
